pr_title: Fix #852 - record deserialized objects before deserialization has completed
pr_body:
This fix for #852 is based on @gabikliot's suggestions in that thread.
I have also included @galvesribeiro's tests for that bug. @galvesribeiro's test uses generated code, unlike the existing `SerializationTests_RecursiveSerialization`. I am not sure if the latter should be kept given it needed to be modified to pass the test.
pr_comments:
Looks good in gene. I can do a detailed code review now.
The previous test has value in that it is standalone, without grains, thus easier to test, repro,  etc... Pure serializer test and not whole system test. Unit test and not integration test, by @Yevhen methodology. No hurm in having both tests I think.
Meant to write: I can not do a detailed code review now.
Thank you, @gabikliot :) I am happy to keep both, too.
I'll kick off a functional run with it to see if anything got broken.
Thanks @ReubenBond  :)

issue_context.title: Bug in DeserializationContext about deserializing cyclic data structures
issue_context.body:
Issue #843 exposed 2 bugs in the serializer related to cyclic data structures (data structure that has a cycle of references).
The first, minor bug, was related to capturing the right offset during serialization of cyclic data structures. It has been fixed in #851.
The 2nd bug is related to Deserialization.
Currently, when we deserialize an object, we first call its generated deserialization method, which will create an empty object and then recursively call deserialization on its member fields and assign them to the object fields. Only after the object was fully deserialized and created, do we put it in the [`DeserializationContext`](https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/blob/master/src/Orleans/Serialization/DeserializationContext.cs#L54). This works if the same object is referenced multiple times from the same parent object (not within a cycle), since when we encounter the same object reference again, it will be found in the [`DeserializationContext`](https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/blob/master/src/Orleans/Serialization/DeserializationContext.cs#L60).

However, it does not work for cyclic objects, since when we encounter a 2nd reference to the same object, the parent object (the first reference to that object in the cycle) was not fully deserialized yet (we are currently deserializing it). As a result, it was not put yet in the `DeserializationContext` and thus cannot be found by the 2nd reference.

The suggested fix is to change the order of deserialization and storing of the object in the `DeserializationContext`. We should first allocate a new empty object, then store a reference to it in the `DeserializationContext` and only then recursively call deserialization on its fields. When storing in the `DeserializationContext` we should store at the `var start = stream.CurrentPosition;` offset like done now [here](https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/blob/master/src/Orleans/Serialization/SerializationManager.cs#L1309). The call to `DeserializationContext.Current.RecordObject` will be removed from [`SerializationManager`](https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/blob/master/src/Orleans/Serialization/SerializationManager.cs#L1309) and instead moved into the generated serialization code, right after the un-initialized object is created.

review_comments: This is referenced from generated code in order to record the object currently being deserialized.
